mission.title: Our Mission
mission.desc: We believe that file sharing should be simple, secure, and private. In an age where digital privacy is constantly under threat, CloudDrop provides a sanctuary for your data. We don't store your files; we simply provide the secure tunnel for them to travel.

why.title: Why CloudDrop?
why.noStorageDesc: Your files go directly from device A to device B.
why.e2eeDesc: Not even we can see what you are sending.
why.noLimitsDesc: Send files of any size, as long as your browser can handle it.
why.openSourceDesc: Trust through transparency. Our code is open for anyone to audit.

openSource.title: Open Source
openSource.desc: CloudDrop is proudly open source. You can view our source code, contribute, or report issues on

zeroKnowledge.title: Zero-Knowledge Architecture
zeroKnowledge.desc: We cannot read your files. We don't want to. CloudDrop is designed so that the server only facilitates the connection setup (Signaling), but the data transfer happens directly between devices (Peer-to-Peer).

e2ee.title: End-to-End Encryption
e2ee.desc: Every file is encrypted in the browser before it is sent and decrypted only after it is received. We use standard, audit-proven cryptographic algorithms:
e2ee.integrity: Integrity: Authenticated encryption ensures data hasn't been tampered with.

p2p.title: Peer-to-Peer (WebRTC)
p2p.desc: CloudDrop utilizes WebRTC to create a direct data channel between peers. This means in most cases, your file data never touches a server, even in encrypted form. It flows directly from your device to the recipient's device through the shortest network path.

q1.question: Is there a file size limit?
q1.answer: No. Since CloudDrop transfers files directly between devices (P2P), there is no arbitrary file size limit imposed by us. The only limit is your browser's capability and your device's available storage.

q2.question: Are my files stored on a server?
q2.answer: No. CloudDrop uses WebRTC for peer-to-peer transfer. Files are streamed directly from the sender to the receiver. We never store your files.

q3.question: Is it secure?
q3.answer: Yes. All transfers are encrypted using DTLS (Datagram Transport Layer Security) via WebRTC. Additionally, we use end-to-end encryption for file content to ensure privacy.

q4.question: Why can't I connect to another device?
q4.answer: Ensure both devices are on the same network or have internet access. If you are on a restrictive network (like a corporate firewall), connection might fail. Try refreshing the room code.

intro.title: 1. Introduction
intro.desc1: Welcome to CloudDrop. By using our website and services, you agree to these Terms of Service. Please read them carefully.
intro.desc2: CloudDrop is a decentralized, peer-to-peer (P2P) file sharing tool. We provide the platform for direct device-to-device communication without server-side storage.

service.title: 2. Service Nature
service.p1: No Storage: CloudDrop does not store your files. All data is transferred directly between users' browsers.
service.p2: Encryption: While we use End-to-End Encryption (E2EE), you understand that no transmission over the internet can be guaranteed as 100% secure.

responsibility.title: 3. User Responsibility
responsibility.p1: You are solely responsible for the content you share through CloudDrop.
responsibility.p2: You agree not to use the service to transfer any content that is illegal, infringing, or harmful.

prohibited.title: 4. Prohibited Activities
prohibited.item1: Violate any local, state, or international laws.
prohibited.item2: Distribute malware, viruses, or any other harmful code.
prohibited.item3: Infringe upon the intellectual property rights of others.

disclaimer.title: 5. Disclaimer of Warranties
disclaimer.desc: CloudDrop is provided "AS IS" and "AS AVAILABLE" without any warranties of any kind. We do not warrant that the service will be uninterrupted or error-free.

liability.title: 6. Limitation of Liability
liability.desc: To the maximum extent permitted by law, CloudDrop and its contributors shall not be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages resulting from the use of the service.

intro.title: How CloudDrop Works
intro.desc: CloudDrop is designed with a single goal: to transfer your files securely without anyone else seeing them. This report explains how we achieve this using modern web technologies.

architecture.title: System Architecture
architecture.desc: Unlike traditional file sharing services, CloudDrop doesn't have a central cloud storage. Instead, it creates a direct pipe between your devices.

step1.title: 1. Discovery
step1.desc: Devices find each other using a 'Room Code' via our signaling server. Note: The server only matches the codes; it never sees your files.

step2.title: 2. Connection
step2.desc: A direct Peer-to-Peer (P2P) connection is established using WebRTC. This is like a private tunnel between the two devices.

step3.title: 3. Encryption
step3.desc: Before leaving your device, the file is encrypted. It travels through the tunnel and is only decrypted when it arrives at the other end.

points.title: Zero Knowledge
points.desc: We don't know what you are sending. The keys stay in your browser.

points.title: Ephemeral
points.desc: No account, no history. Once you close the tab, the connection data is erased.

points.title: Client-Side
points.desc: All processing happens locally. Your privacy is enforced by math, not promises.
